topic_and_scope: A hospital-based study from Southwest Ethiopia assessing CKD prevalence and predictors among HAART-naïve and HAART-experienced HIV-infected adults, highlighting associations with anemia, hypertension, obesity, water intake, and WHO clinical stage. The work underscores limitations of cross-sectional design and CKD assessment methods, pointing to the need for longitudinal and methodologically rigorous follow-up to inform care and policy.
main_themes: CKD prevalence and ART exposure status
Modifiable and non-modifiable CKD risk factors in PLHIV
Measurement, methods, and policy implications for CKD in HIV care
main_findings: Overall CKD prevalence was 19.3% (119/616); CKD was more prevalent among HAART-naïve patients (29.3%) than HAART-experienced patients (16.4%).

Distinct predictors by ART status: among naïve patients, rural residence, anemia, hypertension, family history of kidney disease, and stage IV WHO clinical stage were independently associated with CKD; among experienced patients, rural residence, low daily water intake, anemia, hypertension, obesity, stage IV WHO stage, and abnormal waist circumference were significant predictors.

key_gaps.description: The cross-sectional design prevents causal or temporal inferences about the relationships between ART exposure, CKD onset/progression, and predictors.
CKD assessment relied on dipstick proteinuria and creatinine-based eGFR with race adjustment, lacking albuminuria (ACR) and cystatin C measurements, which may bias CKD classification and staging.

future_directions.title: Establish a prospective cohort to measure CKD incidence and progression in PLHIV starting ART
future_directions.rationale: To determine temporal and causal relationships between ART initiation/changes and CKD development. A longitudinal cohort should enroll HAART-naïve individuals at ART initiation and follow them with regular assessments (eGFR, albuminuria via ACR, cystatin C, blood pressure, anemia status, BMI) for 2–5 years. Stratify by ART regimen and adherence, CD4 count, and viral load to identify regimen-specific renal outcomes and modifiers. This design will address the key limitation of cross-sectional data and help define optimal monitoring intervals and protective factors.

future_directions.title: Compare nephrotoxicity across ART regimens with robust renal phenotyping
future_directions.rationale: The observed differences in CKD by ART exposure may reflect nephrotoxic effects of certain drugs (e.g., TDF) or broader effects of viral suppression. A study should compare regimens (TDF- vs non-TDF-containing, DTG-based vs PI-based, etc.) using repeated kidney function tests, tubular biomarkers, eGFR trajectories, and albuminuria. Adjust for baseline kidney health, age, hypertension, diabetes, BMI, and anemia. Findings will inform regimen selection and kidney monitoring guidelines in PLHIV.

future_directions.title: Implement and evaluate routine CKD screening in ART clinics
future_directions.rationale: Given CKD prevalence and its impact on outcomes, a standardized screening protocol (annual eGFR with CKD-EPI, ACR for albuminuria, and basic metabolic panel) should be piloted in ART clinics. Include training, data capture, and cost-effectiveness analysis. Outcomes to monitor include stage at diagnosis, time to treatment of comorbidities, ART management changes, and CKD progression over time. This would provide evidence for policy adoption and resource allocation.

future_directions.title: Test hydration interventions to reduce CKD risk in rural PLHIV
future_directions.rationale: Low daily water intake was linked to CKD among experienced patients, possibly via effects on stone formation or renal perfusion. A cluster-randomized trial in rural clinics could test promoting water consumption to meet WHO guidelines, with endpoints including CKD incidence, urinary indices, and BP control. Monitoring adherence and potential confounders (diet, NSAID use, herbal medicines) will help determine feasibility and potential population-level impact.

future_directions.title: Evaluate obesity management as a CKD risk-reduction strategy in ART-experienced HIV patients
future_directions.rationale: Obesity was associated with CKD among experienced participants. Implement and evaluate a lifestyle intervention (nutrition counseling, physical activity, behavioral support) integrated into HIV care to reduce BMI and waist circumference. Assess effects on renal outcomes (eGFR slope, albuminuria), blood pressure, glucose tolerance, and lipid profiles over 12–24 months. This could inform non-pharmacologic CKD prevention in this population.

future_directions.title: Investigate anemia management and its effect on CKD trajectories in PLHIV
future_directions.rationale: Anemia was a strong predictor of CKD in both naïve and experienced groups. A trial or quasi-experimental study evaluating anemia treatment (iron supplementation where indicated, erythropoiesis-stimulating agents where appropriate) alongside ART optimization could determine whether correcting anemia slows CKD progression. Outcomes would include changes in Hgb, eGFR, and proteinuria, adjusting for iron studies and inflammatory status.

future_directions.title: Address rural-urban disparities with community-based CKD risk-reduction programs
future_directions.rationale: Rural residence consistently predicted CKD risk. Develop and evaluate community-level interventions—education on CKD risk factors, improved access to screening, safer use of traditional medicines, and stronger linkage to care. Measure downstream effects on CKD awareness, detection rates, treatment initiation for hypertension/anemia, and renal outcomes in rural PLHIV.

future_directions.title: Validate and update CKD risk prediction in PLHIV with enhanced biomarker-based measures
future_directions.rationale: The current model used traditional risk factors; external validation in diverse Ethiopian settings is needed. Incorporate albuminuria (ACR), cystatin C-based eGFR where feasible, and consider region-specific factors (nutrition, water quality, herbal exposure). Develop a locally calibrated risk score for early CKD detection and targeted monitoring in ART programs.
